purpose: Planning and reference rules for targeted normalization and taxonomy refinement after the 50-case DeepSeek pilot error analysis. This file documents intended label decisions before changing prompts, model code, golden labels, or evaluation logic.

store_location: Extract the complete store name from the subject or body whenever it appears explicitly.
Prefer the full branch name, for example Hangzhou West Lake Store rather than Hangzhou or West Lake.
Use unknown only when no store location is explicitly stated and no store location is reasonably inferable.
If the model predicts a city-only or branch-only name, normalize it to the full known store name when the mapping is unambiguous.
sentiment: Use positive for praise or satisfaction without an unresolved problem.
Use neutral for information requests, general inquiries, or mixed wording without a clear complaint or unresolved issue.
Use negative for explicit complaints, unresolved issues, refund or exchange requests caused by a problem, product defects, service failures, delivery failures, or safety and health concerns.
If an email contains praise but also asks for help with an unresolved issue, default to negative unless the issue is only a minor neutral inquiry.
urgency: Use high only for safety or health concern, urgent or ASAP language, immediate action requests, repeated long-term no response, severe disruption, or strong escalation language.
Use medium for unresolved refund or exchange requests, delivery delay, repeated contact without severe urgency cues, and standard complaints needing follow-up.
Use low for praise, neutral inquiry, or minor issue without time pressure.
is_complaint: Use true when the email contains an explicit complaint, unresolved issue, refund/exchange request caused by a problem, product defect, service failure, delivery failure, or safety/health concern.
Use false for praise, neutral inquiry, or general information request without an unresolved problem.
If sentiment is negative because of a customer problem, is_complaint should usually be true.
product_category: Use the closest allowed product category from the project taxonomy.
Do not invent new product category labels during evaluation.
Use Other only when the product cannot reasonably fit Electronics, Home Appliances, Clothing, Furniture, Beauty Products, Sportswear, or Service.
complaint_reason: Use refund request if the customer explicitly requests refund, refund me, money back, or direct reimbursement.
Use after-sales service if the issue is exchange, warranty, return policy, replacement, repair, or post-purchase handling.
Use customer service if the issue is no support response, poor support communication, call/email/chat not followed up, or service team communication failure.
Use delivery delay if shipment is delayed, delivery update is confusing, delivery status is wrong, or logistics handling is the main issue.
Use product quality if the main issue is defect, malfunction, damaged product, missing part, or general product quality.
Use health or safety issue when the product creates a health, safety, irritation, injury, or risk concern.
Use none for praise or neutral inquiry without complaint.
Use other only when none of the defined categories can reasonably apply.
source_attribution: Identify the main business source of the complaint, not legal liability.
Use one primary label unless a future schema adds multi-label attribution.
Use none for non-complaint praise or neutral inquiry.
Use unclear only when the business source cannot be identified from the email.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: product issue
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The root cause is product quality, product defect, missing part, malfunction, damaged product, or safety-related product problem.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: delivery/logistics issue
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The issue is late delivery, confusing delivery update, missing shipment, wrong delivery status, or logistics handling.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: customer service response issue
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The issue is no reply, no follow-up, delayed support response, phone/email/chat support failure, or service team communication failure.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: store service issue
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The issue happened in a physical store or with in-store staff handling, and the core problem is staff or store process behavior rather than refund/exchange policy.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: refund/exchange process issue
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The core user request is refund, exchange, return, warranty, replacement, repair, or policy/process handling.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: none
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The email is positive praise or a neutral inquiry without a complaint.

source_attribution_priority_rules.label: unclear
source_attribution_priority_rules.use_when: The source cannot be identified from the email.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: health or safety issue
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The customer reports health, safety, injury, irritation, risk, burning smell, overheating, or other safety-related harm.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: refund request
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The customer explicitly requests refund, refund me, money back, or direct reimbursement.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: wrong item
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The delivered or received item is different from what the customer ordered.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: delivery delay
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The shipment is delayed, the delivery update is confusing, or delivery/logistics status is the central problem.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: product quality
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The product is defective, damaged, malfunctioning, missing parts, or has poor quality.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: customer service
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The main issue is no support response, poor communication, or missing phone/email/chat follow-up.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: after-sales service
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: The issue is exchange, warranty, return policy, replacement, repair, or post-purchase handling without an explicit refund request.

complaint_reason_priority_rules.label: other
complaint_reason_priority_rules.use_when: No defined complaint reason can reasonably apply.

sentiment_mixed_feedback_rule.positive: Praise or satisfaction without unresolved problem.
sentiment_mixed_feedback_rule.neutral: Information request, general inquiry, or mixed wording without clear complaint or unresolved issue.
sentiment_mixed_feedback_rule.negative: Explicit complaint, unresolved issue, refund/exchange request caused by a problem, product defect, service failure, delivery failure, or safety/health concern.
sentiment_mixed_feedback_rule.default_for_praise_plus_unresolved_issue: negative unless the issue is only a minor neutral inquiry

high: urgent, ASAP, immediately, or equivalent wording
medium: repeated contact without severe urgency cues

store_location_extraction_rule.primary_rule: Extract the complete store name from subject or body whenever present.
store_location_extraction_rule.unknown_rule: Use unknown only when no store location is explicitly or reasonably inferable.

examples.observed_issue: The email explicitly asks for a refund because an issue remains unresolved. DeepSeek predicted after-sales service and customer service response issue, while golden labels used refund request and refund/exchange process issue.
examples.rule_decision: Prefer complaint_reason=refund request and source_attribution=refund/exchange process issue when the core user request is refund or money back.
examples.review_note: Urgency medium is reasonable unless the text includes urgent, ASAP, safety, or repeated long-term no-response cues.

examples.observed_issue: The full store name Hangzhou West Lake Store appears in the body, but prediction used unknown. The issue involves no follow-up after contacting the service desk.
examples.rule_decision: Extract full store name when present. Use source_attribution=customer service response issue for no follow-up or no response.
examples.review_note: Urgency high requires stronger cue than two contacts unless the project treats repeated no follow-up as escalation.

examples.observed_issue: The body mentions Nanjing Xinjiekou Store and a desk lamp, but prediction returned unknown store and Electronics category.
examples.rule_decision: Normalize complete store location from text and keep desk lamp as Furniture. Staff not recording a complaint may be store service or customer service depending on annotation policy.
examples.review_note: This is a boundary case between store staff handling and customer service response.

examples.observed_issue: The email praises the rice cooker but asks for help because the delivery update was confusing. Prediction used neutral and delivery/logistics issue, while golden labels used negative and unclear.
examples.rule_decision: For praise plus unresolved issue, default sentiment to negative unless it is only a minor inquiry. Delivery update confusion should generally map to delivery delay or delivery/logistics issue unless the source is genuinely unclear.
examples.review_note: This case should be manually reviewed because it exposes golden-label boundary tension.

examples.observed_issue: The email praises the product fit but still needs help because exchange policy was unclearly explained by staff.
examples.rule_decision: Use negative for praise plus unresolved issue. Prefer complaint_reason=after-sales service and source_attribution=refund/exchange process issue when exchange policy is central.
examples.review_note: If the focus is staff explanation rather than policy handling, store service issue may also be plausible.

implementation_notes: This config is a planning/reference artifact and is not yet automatically enforced by the model chain.
Do not change existing golden labels automatically based on this file.
Use this file to guide later prompt revision, output normalization, and golden-label review.
The current schema remains single-label for complaint_reason and source_attribution, so mixed cases require a primary-label decision.
